chapter: Small group, new sound and Europe
title: First European tour
summary: He describes the thrill of the 1954 trip, the reception, and the 1957 Royal Command Performance.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. I would like to ask Freddie what his first impressions were when he went abroad -- when the band went abroad for the first time, Stan.
Uh-huh.
Which was '54.
Very, very exciting as far as I'm concerned.
Was it?
Oh, yeah.
Did you go to England first, or to the Continent first?
I think we went to the Continent first.
I think so.
I think we went to the Continent first, because they had an exchange with two bands, or something like that. We wanted to go to England first, you know --
Yeah.
-- but, we had to go to the Continent first. And, then we finally went on into England. But, I really loved --
I think you came to England first --
Huh?
You must have come to England first, because I remember Basie said to me -- he came with Lockjaw -- and he said -- "He's been talking to me all the way from Idlewild to here".
(laugh)
He says -- "Now you've got him".
(laugh)
That's the first time I met Lockjaw,
Oh, yeah? I wonder --
I think that must have been '54.
It says -- "In '54 when the band made it's first tour of Europe...". "In '55 when Basie completed his 20th year...
No. I think it was later. I think we were married then. Oh, well we were married then.
Oh, sure. This is correct. Well, anyway, I mean, that's immaterial, because we know about who the band was, and I just wanted to see how it affected everybody.

Oh, listen. The European trip was -- affected -- really affected everybody -- everybody was looking forward to it, you know -- going over there. We had been trying to get there for years, you know. The [whole] band
Yeah.
And, we finally got a chance to go there, so for me it was a big thrill.
Yeah. Yeah.
You know.
And, it must have been a big thrill for Basie.
Oh, I'm sure it was.
I mean, he had a tremendous reception.
Yes. Yes.
Yeah.
Unbelievable reception that we got over there.
And, also they played a Command Performance, -- Stan, -- in --
Not in '54.
-- no, not in '54. I think it was in '57. 'First U.S. band ever to play a Royal Command Performance'.
Mm hmm.
Yeah. '57 I think -- which must have been a thrill.
It was. Oh, it was. Yeah, it was something.
